title: July 2026 Leadership Update - All Hands

transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-07-06 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~75 minutes | Attendees: Evelyn, Daniel, Lena, Marcus, Priya, Omar + company
[00:00] Evelyn: ok hey everyone welcome to the July leadership update, um we're gonna kick off with Q2 highlights, super proud of the team, but a few things to call out.
[00:12] Daniel: Quick note, audio might be a little fuzzy for remote folks, sorry about that.
[00:16] Evelyn: No worries. Alright so Q2 in one slide — usage up 42% quarter over quarter, revenue runway looks healthy, but unit costs are still higher than we expected on inference.
[00:30] Lena: Yeah, the cost is mainly in bursty workloads and some suboptimal batching on a few customers. We shipped new batching heuristics in May that have started to show results but haven't fully ramped.
[00:42] Marcus: To add — we're rolling out KV cache improvements that reduce repeated prefix work, that should help tail latency as well. There's a note in the engineering channel about kernel selector changes.
[00:55] Evelyn: Good. On product: Dedicated capacity growth is strong, customers like the predictability, but we still hear requests for better autoscaling and easier private deployment setup.
[01:08] Lena: Roadmap — Dedicated: Q3 focus is autoscaling improvements and smoother burst to public fallback. Private: we're targeting GA for the VPC-managed control plane in late Q3, with an on-prem packaging pilot earlier.
[01:22] Employee 1: Sorry can you repeat the Private GA date?
[01:25] Lena: late Q3, leaning toward end of September; we still have a few compliance items (KMS integrations, audit log polishing) to close.
[01:34] Priya: From customer conversations, security and audit logs are frequently a gating item for mid-market and enterprise buyers. We continue to push SOC2 type stuff and ISO questions.
[01:45] Evelyn: Yes, SOC2 is our next milestone for the august audit cycle; Omar and security will share more after this.
[01:52] Omar: We'll publish the compliance timeline in #security by EOD tomorrow, also working on more detailed KMS/HSM integration notes for external partners.
[02:03] Employee 2: What about the hiring freeze rumor? Is that real?
[02:06] Evelyn: Good question — no company-wide freeze. We're being more deliberate: some teams have pauses, others keep hiring for critical roles. Priya will send a clear breakdown.
[02:17] Priya: Correct — sales/solutions hiring continues for enterprise motion; product/infra open reqs prioritized but interviews may be slower as we calibrate budgets.
[02:28] Daniel: Technical update — we've seen two notable infra incidents in May/June, both related to autoscaler edge cases and a dependency issue with our cloud provider. We've made a fix to the autoscaler algorithm and added more probing before scale-down.
[02:40] Marcus: There's also a perf project to reduce per-token CPU overhead by switching some matmul ops to fused kernels, early results show 10-15% CPU reduction on 8k context.
[02:52] Employee 3: Any ETA on when those perf gains reach Hosted API?
[02:56] Marcus: We hope to roll gradual changes in canary in the next 6 weeks; will start with non-critical models and measure regressions.
[03:05] Lena: On the product roadmap slide — we plan a new Optimize feature for automated batching suggestions and model quantization recommendations by workload; early beta with select customers in August.
[03:18] Evelyn: This ties to our quality monitoring stack too — we'll link evals and regression alerts so customers can see when a model change degrades a prompt set.
[03:28] Q&A segment starts
[03:30] Employee 4: Will Dedicated get same SLAs as Hosted?
[03:33] Priya: Dedicated has SLA tiers based on committed capacity; higher tiers will include tighter latency SLOs and a faster incident response. Details will be in the customer SLAs doc.
[03:44] Employee 5: Are we still supporting on-prem for highly regulated customers?
[03:47] Lena: Yes, on-prem remains an option for the pilot customers; though the default is VPC-managed Private for most enterprises. On-prem packaging will be more manual initially.
[03:55] Employee 6: How are we handling competitor positioning — heard MajorCloudAI rolled out a new price war promotion.
[03:59] Evelyn: We're focusing on serving economics and predictability as our differentiation — it's not just price, it's latency, reliability, and operational tooling. We'll keep watching price movements.
[04:12] Daniel: also there are some new OSS inference runtimes — we should keep up with kernel work and quantization profiles so we don't fall behind.
[04:20] Marcus: Action items assigned: scheduling, postmortems, and roadmap docs.
[04:26] Employee 7: small nit — the product name on the slides says 'Redwood Dedicate' in one place, typo?
[04:30] Lena: oh yeah thanks, we'll correct to 'Redwood Dedicated' before sharing.
[04:34] Evelyn: Ok final remarks — thank you all, Q3 is gonna be execution heavy but we're in a good spot. We'll share the deck and a few follow-ups: hiring breakdown, Private GA checklist, Dedicated deep-dive invite.
[04:49] Meeting ends
Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-heard words and typos typical of automated captions, proper nouns may be slightly off. Links referenced: https://redwoodinternal.company/q2-deck (company-internal link), https://redwoodinternal.company/dedicated-deep-dive-invite
